name: prime_phase_nat_remainder468
twin: For every prime and modulus at least two, the phase at a over q plus z is the phase at a times the natural remainder over q times the phase at z.
source: Page 155 equation 2.3. Exact residue phase identity used before the character expansion.
instance: q two, a one, z zero and prime three give negative one on both sides.

name: prime_phase_periodic442_counterexample468
twin: At q two, a one, z zero and prime three, the sealed formula with real field remainder has unequal sides. Its left side is negative one and its right side is one.
source: Annotation audit of page 155 equation 2.3. This is a Lean statement audit and no claim of a paper error.
instance: The natural number three is prime. The modulus two meets the lower bound.

name: prime_class_series_summable442
twin: The damped prime Fourier series restricted to any residue class is absolutely summable when N is at least one.
source: Page 155 equation 2.3. The restriction of the damped prime series of page 154.
instance: N one, q two, b one and z zero give the odd prime series with nonzero term exp of negative three.

name: prime_class_phase_series_summable442
twin: The restricted prime series stays absolutely summable after multiplying every term by its constant class phase.
source: Page 155 equation 2.3. The residue phase multiplying the inner class series.
instance: N one, q two, a one, b one and z zero give the odd prime series multiplied by negative one.

name: prime_fourier_class_collapse442
twin: The shifted damped prime series equals the prime sum of the finite sum of its residue class terms. Each inner sum has exactly one eligible residue.
source: Page 155 equation 2.3. Splitting the prime index by residue before separating the noncoprime error.
instance: N one, q two, a one and z zero have a nonzero term at prime two in class zero and a nonzero term at prime three in class one.

name: prime_fourier_class_interchange442
twin: The absolutely convergent prime sum and the finite sum over the q residue classes can be interchanged.
source: Page 155 equation 2.3. Regrouping the absolutely convergent damped prime series.
instance: N one, q two, a one and z zero give two nonempty residue classes, containing prime two and prime three.

name: prime_class_phase_factor442
twin: The constant phase of a residue class factors out of its damped prime series.
source: Page 155 equation 2.3. The constant class phase in front of the inner prime series.
instance: N one, q two, a one, b one and z zero give the constant negative one times the nonempty odd prime series.
